prompt:
Scene:
Same square frame, same canyon, same camera position and lens as the reference. Time is now pre-dawn blue hour — cool cyan sky with a pale warm band rising on the left horizon. Cold temperature suggested by condensation haze filling the lower canyon.

Subject:
The identical rising water column from the reference (same base position, same 600-meter height, same plume profile, same bloom height). Because of the cold pre-dawn air, the column now sheds a dense white mist that rolls sideways off its surface and descends slowly back into the canyon, pooling as fog along the river below. The helicopter scale anchor remains in the same mid-height position.

Important details:
Preserve the column base location, diameter, and overall silhouette. Cool palette: indigo canyon shadows, silver mist, hints of warm peach near the horizon. The mist obscures some canyon wall detail but the rising column must remain clearly readable. Condensation halo at the top becomes a wide diffuse aurora-like cloud from mixed vapor and cold. Sandstone stays identifiable in the sunlit upper rim.

Use case:
Second image in the cycle. Confirms the queue can treat 01 as --ref while swapping time of day and atmospheric moisture.

Constraints:
PRESERVE the reference image canyon geometry, column base and silhouette, river course, and helicopter position. No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no rain, no wind-tilted column, no stylized illustration.
